headline: Referred red light camera ordinance to City Council with “speed” removed; flood damage code amendments sent to Council for adoption.
summary: Public comments focused on red light cameras, including who gets a ticket when someone else drives and how fines are used. Members voted to remove the word “speed” from the red light ordinance and send it to the City Council. They also referred flood damage prevention amendments to the City Council for adoption.
decisions: Approved the minutes of August 4, 2026, by motion, with one member recused.
Referred amendments to Code Section Appendix D, Flood Damage Prevention, to the City Council for adoption, unanimously.
Zoning Commission put an 18-month moratorium on vape shops, except for applications already pending.
Removed the word “speed” from the red light ordinance and referred it to the City Council for a Motion to Introduce, unanimously.
Changed “Automated Traffic Enforcement Safety Devices” to “Automated Red Light Traffic Enforcement Safety Devices” in the ordinance, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Councilman Seymour made a motion to approve the minutes of August 4, 2026, seconded by Chairman Dickau. Councilwoman Tyler recused herself as she didn’t attend the last meeting - Motion passed.
Councilman Seymour made a motion to refer this matter to the City Council for adoption, seconded by Councilwoman Tyler. All present voted in favor – Motion passed.
Chairman Dickau stated that the Zoning Commission has put an 18 month moratorium on vape shops, except for people who have an application currently pending.

The Committee discussed the red light ordinance that had recently passed and decided to remove the word “speed” from the language. Councilman Seymour made a motion to remove the language and refer to the City Council for a Motion to Introduce, seconded by Chairman Dickau. All present voted in favor – Motion passed.

Councilman Seymour made a motion change Automated Traffic Enforcement Safety Devices to Automated Red Light Traffic Enforcement Safety Devices, seconded by Chairman Dickau. All present voted in favor – Motion passed.

plain_text:
ORDINANCE COMMITTEE 
TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 1, 2026 
CITY HALL, ROOM 1-1 
111 NORTH MAIN STREET 
 
 
 
 
ATTENDEES: Mark Dickau, Susan Tyler and Steve Seymour 
ABSENT:   None. 
STAFF PRESENT: Jeffrey R. Steeg, Assistant Corporation Counsel                                                                    
   Noelle Bates, Recording Secretary 
1.  Call to Order 
 The Ordinance Committee was called to order at 5:00 p.m. by Chairman Dickau.  All in 
attendance stood for the Pledge of Allegiance. 
2. Approval of Minutes 
 a.  August 4, 2026 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to approve the minutes of August 4, 2026, seconded 
by Chairman Dickau.  Councilwoman Tyler recused herself as she didn’t attend the last 
meeting - Motion passed. 
3.  Public Participation 
Nicholas Palmer, 69 Cronin Street read a statement into the record which is attached to these 
minutes.  He is not in favor or the red light cameras. 
Amy Paris, 82 Stafford Avenue, #38 stated that she was against the red light cameras and she 
feels there is too much surveillance. 
Patrick Parenti, 281 Wolcott Street stated that he was in favor of the red light cameras.  He stated 
that red light cameras aren’t the only devices that are recording people. 
Marian Sirois, 362 Shrub Road stated that she had a question regarding the language and asked 
why there was “speed” cameras in the language.  Chairman Dickau told her that he stated in the 
beginning of the meeting that they would not be addressing that issue. 
Sarah Pagano, 15 Irving Street had a question as to who gets a ticket if someone else is driving 
your vehicle?  She also stated that she believes that people’s driving has gotten worse since we 
legalized marijuana. 
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu spoke to address people’s concerns.  She stated that the ordinance has 
already passed and has been adopted.  The Board of Police Commissioners referred the 
ordinance to this committee to remove the word “speed”.
She continued to say that there was an appeal process for any owner that received a ticket when 
someone else was driving their vehicle.  
She also addressed the issue about the revenue from the cameras.  She stated that any funds 
received by the City from fines imposed pursuant to the ordinance shall be used for the purposes 
of improving transportation mobility, investing in transportation infrastructure improvements, or 
paying the costs associated with the use of Automated Red Light Traffic Enforcement Safety 
Devices within Bristol. 
Lastly the Mayor stated that they haven’t picked a vendor yet but have reached out to 7 of them.  
The City will be conducting a public meeting so everyone can ask the vendors their questions. 
Chairman Dickau read emails from Hal Kilby, 651 Lake Avenue, Bob & Patti Kalat, 34 Holley 
Rd., Ernie Pitti, 65 Palmorr Place, all of which were in favor of the red light cameras.  A copy of 
those emails are attached to the minutes. 
4.  Old Business 
 a.  Review of amendments and report from public hearing on Code Section Appendix D – 
Flood Damage Prevention 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to refer this matter to the City Council for adoption, 
seconded by Councilwoman Tyler.   All present voted in favor – Motion passed. 
 b.  Update on Vape Retailers – Zoning Commission discussion 
Chairman Dickau stated that the Zoning Commission has put an 18 month moratorium on vape 
shops, except for people who have an application currently pending.  There will be a Public 
Comment meeting on September 21st at the Zoning Commission hearing. 
5. New Business 
The Committee discussed the red light ordinance that had recently passed and decided to remove 
the word “speed” from the language. 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to remove the language and refer to the City Council 
for a Motion to Introduce, seconded by Chairman Dickau.   All present voted in favor – 
Motion passed. 
Councilman Seymour made a motion change Automated Traffic Enforcement Safety 
Devices to Automated Red Light Traffic Enforcement Safety Devices, seconded by 
Chairman Dickau.   All present voted in favor – Motion passed.
6.  Additional Public Participation 
None. 
7.  Committee Member Comments 
None. 
8.  Adjournment 
Councilman Seymour made a motion to adjourn at 5:39 p.m., seconded by Councilwoman 
Tyler.   All present voted in favor – Motion passed. 
Respectfully submitted,                                                                                                               
Noelle Bates                                                                                                                                                                                 
Recording Secretary
